w: Two residential towers in Porta Nuova wear a forest instead of a facade - over ninety plant species growing up walls that reach 116 metres. Boeri Studio's 2014 vertical-greening experiment won the International Highrise Award, then was named the world's most beautiful and innovative skyscraper by tall-building experts.
s: Two skyscrapers wearing a forest instead of walls
_facts: Complex of two residential skyscrapers by Boeri Studio in Porta Nuova, Milan, heights 116m and 84m
Over ninety plant species, including tall shrubs and trees, distributed on the facades
Inaugurated 2014; won the International Highrise Award 2014
Named 'most beautiful and innovative skyscraper in the world' by the Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat in 2015

w: When Milan's cemetery ran out of room in 1210, the overflow got its own chapel - walls packed with human skulls and bones. A church grew around the ossuary in 1269, burned down in 1712, and was rebuilt bigger, leaving one of the city's stranger side chapels intact behind the altar.
s: A chapel walled floor to ceiling in human bones
_facts: Church in Milan best known for its ossuary, a side chapel decorated with numerous human skulls and bones
In 1210 an adjacent cemetery ran out of space, so a room was built to hold bones
A church was attached in 1269, renovated in 1679, destroyed by fire in 1712
A new, bigger church was then attached, dedicated to Saint Bernardino of Siena

w: Opened in 1866 to gather Milan's scattered graveyards into one, the Cimitero Monumentale reads like an open-air sculpture park - Greek temples, obelisks, a scaled-down Trajan's Column, tombs by Fontana and Ponti. Its Famedio hall of fame holds novelist Alessandro Manzoni; a BBPR memorial marks 800 camp dead.
s: An open-air sculpture park built for the dead
_facts: One of the two largest cemeteries in Milan, noted for its abundance of artistic tombs and monuments
Designed by Carlo Maciachini, officially opened 1866, consolidating scattered smaller cemeteries
Features Greek temples, obelisks and a scaled-down version of Trajan's Column; tombs by Lucio Fontana, Gio Ponti, and others
Main entrance through the Famedio, holding the tomb of novelist Alessandro Manzoni
A memorial by the BBPR group marks about 800 Milanese killed in Nazi concentration camps

w: One of Milan's oldest churches started in Roman times, rebuilt so often since that art historians call it a building of 'daring originality.' It stands by the old Porta Ticinese and the Roman columns of the Colonne di San Lorenzo - the closest thing left to churches Constantine's successors built in Byzantium.
s: One of Milan's oldest churches, rebuilt for centuries
_facts: One of the oldest churches in Milan, originally built in Roman times, rebuilt several times over the centuries
Located near the medieval Porta Ticinese and the Roman Colonne di San Lorenzo
Art historians H.W. Janson and Anthony F. Janson call it a building of 'daring originality' that gives a glimpse of churches built by Constantine's successors in Byzantium, none of which stand today

w: BBPR's 106-metre tower went up beside the Duomo in the late 1950s, completed 1958, one of Italy's few true examples of post-rationalist brutalist architecture. It took until 2011 for the city to place it under historic protection, by which point a Missori metro exit was depositing riders directly at its foot.
_facts: Skyscraper built in the 1950s by the BBPR architectural partnership, completed 1958, inaugurated 1961
106 metres tall, 26 stories, considered one of the few Italian examples of post-rationalist brutalist architecture
Located in Milan city centre near the Duomo; one exit of Missori metro station sits right in front of it
Placed under protection as a historic building in 2011

w: Behind the altar of this small Renaissance church is a false apse - a shallow niche painted and carved by Donato Bramante to read as metres of receding space, an early trompe-l'oeil. The church, built 1476-1482, wraps around a much older medieval shrine to Satyrus, Saint Ambrose's own brother.
s: Bramante's optical illusion of an apse
_facts: Italian Renaissance structure built 1476-1482, houses an early medieval shrine to Satyrus, brother of Saint Ambrose
Known for its false apse, an early example of trompe-l'oeil, attributed to Donato Bramante

w: Milan's old military parade ground, the Piazza d'armi, became parkland at the end of the 19th century and now covers 386,000 square metres, fenced and watched by video surveillance. Its name comes from Corso Sempione, the Napoleonic-era road it borders; its Porta Sempione gate is heir to the vanished Porta Giovia.
s: A parade ground turned into Milan's back garden
_facts: Green area built at the end of the 19th century on the area previously occupied by the Piazza d'armi (parade ground)
Covers 386,000 square metres, completely fenced and under video surveillance
Name derives from Corso Sempione, a Napoleonic-era road; the new Porta Sempione is heir to the Porta Giovia

w: Giovanni Muzio's 1933 Palazzo dell'Arte in Parco Sempione has hosted the Milan Triennial exhibition on and off since 1936, and runs a design museum today. Since 2003 it has handed out the Gold Medal for Italian Architecture to names like Renzo Piano and Massimiliano Fuksas.
_facts: Museum of art and design in Parco Sempione, housed in the Palazzo dell'Arte built 1931-1933 by Giovanni Muzio
The Milan Triennial exhibition was held there 13 times between 1936 and 1996, and again in 2016
Since 2003 the Triennale has awarded the Gold Medal for Italian Architecture, recipients including Renzo Piano and Massimiliano Fuksas

n: Museo Civico di Storia Naturale di Milano
w: Dinosaur skeletons share the halls with Italy's largest collection of ecosystem dioramas at Milan's civic natural history museum, a collection spanning geology, plants and animals in one sprawling municipal survey of the natural world.
s: Dinosaurs and dioramas under one civic roof
_facts: Museum dedicated to the study of animals, plants and the natural environment including geology
Exhibits include dinosaurs and Italy's largest collection of dioramas of ecosystems
